title: Ge/ZnS Dual-Band Filter with Wide-Bound Random Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Expanding thickness bounds to [20-450] nm with random midpoint initialization (220 nm ±40%) will enable the optimizer to discover phase-matched configurations that quarter-wave constrained initialization missed, improving best_target_score beyond 0.8679.
design_principle: Transfer matrix method optimization with unconstrained thickness exploration allows discovery of non-quarter-wave solutions that may better satisfy dual-band transmission requirements while maintaining blocking.
proposed_topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 (22 finite layers, 11 Ge + 11 ZnS alternating)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: All thicknesses within [20-450] nm range achievable by PVD
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer propagation
Interference filter theory: alternating high/low index layers create bandpass characteristics
Quarter-wave initialization as starting point but not constraint
expected_advantages: Wider search space may discover superior local optima
Random initialization avoids bias toward quarter-wave solutions
Disabled adaptive step-scaling prevents premature convergence
known_risks: Wider bounds may increase optimization iterations needed
Random initialization may require more rounds to converge
Some thickness combinations may produce high absorption
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer alternating Ge/ZnS dielectric stack on CaF2 substrate for dual-band infrared transmission. Layer sequence: Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS (22 finite layers). Initialize all layer thicknesses with random uniform distribution centered at 220 nm with ±40% variance (range approximately 132-308 nm initial). Set optimization bounds to [20, 450] nm for all 22 thickness variables. Disable adaptive step-scaling for first 50% of optimization budget. Use coherent transfer matrix solver at normal incidence. Wavelength range 2500-5000 nm. Four mean-transmittance objectives: maximize in 3250-3350 nm (methane band), maximize in 4200-4300 nm (CO2 band), minimize in 2500-3100 nm (blocking), minimize in 4450-5000 nm (blocking). Run both gradient_thickness and differential_evolution_thickness optimizers. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Expanded thickness bounds from [80-400] nm to [20-450] nm per feedback directive; replaced quarter-wave constrained initialization with random midpoint distribution (220 nm ±40%); disabled adaptive step-scaling initially to prevent premature convergence to phase-mismatched states observed in iteration_10.
